title: Reviewer quota exhaustion: authorized fallback, no fallback, and anti-shopping
description: The primary reviewer binding cannot execute for an operational reason. Three sub-conditions are judged together: (a) an authorized alternate binding runs the same reviewer contract; (b) with no authorized binding the run stays blocked and no verdict is fabricated; (c) a negative reviewer verdict cannot be re-opened by reporting the binding unavailable.

oracle.judges: Compares the reviewer contract fields across substitution and checks the blocked / anti-shopping sub-conditions against recorded run events.

expected.claim: Fallback may move where a review runs, never what it must satisfy, and never escapes an adverse verdict.

shared.task_inputs: task.md and fixtures/ are byte-identical for both variants.
shared.frozen_check: fixtures/check.sh, frozen before any variant runs.

divergent.evidence_acquisition: The baseline has no notion of a reviewer binding, so it records a verdict without provenance. The exitbind variant records which binding ran and why the primary could not. The oracle judges the recorded contract fields and bounds, not the variant.

threats_to_validity: A baseline cannot express the fallback concept at all; its sub-conditions are therefore recorded as exercised=false and yield inconclusive rather than a fabricated pass.
Whether the alternate host is genuinely independent of the primary is a provider-level claim the oracle cannot verify; it checks only that the binding changed and the contract did not.

sub_scenarios.condition: primary binding cannot execute; an authorized alternate binding is configured
primary binding cannot execute; no alternate binding is authorized
reviewer returned an adverse verdict, then reports its binding unavailable

not_yet_run_reason: Judging this scenario requires recording a live run's reviewer contract fields and event provenance. The fixture double cannot produce a reviewer substitution, so sub-conditions are recorded as exercised=false until an exitbind/baseline adapter exists.
